In ProfileStore._read_from_disk (src/sqllens/profiles.py:159-178), an entry whose body is not a dict (e.g. {"a": 5}) hits `skipped.append(name); continue` at lines 165-167 with no logger call. Only the model_validate failure path (lines 168-178) logs a per-entry line. So the claim that a single entry failing validation is 'logged on its own line' is false for non-object bodies. These entries are still named in load_error (lines 190-202) when all names are valid, so the second half holds. The same gap makes docs line 62 ('named only in their per-entry log lines') wrong for non-dict bodies. A hand-edited profiles file can produce this input.

The first parts hold. Invalid names are skipped (profiles.py:161-164) and set _invalid_profile_names (183). _save raises ProfileNameError (205-209), and upsert/delete both call _save, so all writes are refused. load_error carries only the invalid-name count (184-188). The last clause is wrong. Entries whose body is not a dict are appended to `skipped` at 165-167 with no per-entry log line. Only the ValidationError path (175-178) logs one. When invalid names are also present, the `elif skipped` branch (190) never runs, so a non-dict-body entry is named neither in load_error nor in any log line. The doc says skipped bad-body entries are 'named only in their per-entry log lines', which is untrue for that case. Example input: {"bad name!": {}, "foo": 5}.
